one_line: A shared redirect-rule console for humans and agents to test, audit, reorder, and migrate routing safely.
what_it_does: Manages redirect rules across hosting platforms, simulates requests, detects shadowing, and validates fixes and migrations.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools share the exact routing state with the human UI and make deterministic audit, reorder, and retest workflows materially more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes fifteen registered tools and one shared store for UI and agent mutations.
Frame sheets show a rules table, request simulator, first-match diagnosis, and agent audit/fix workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent deployed console with a concrete routing failure and a visible diagnose/fix/test workflow; the many platform and migration claims are not all independently demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show rules, simulator, audit output, and rule-order correction states.
Facts report a live demo and 148 passing tests.
impact_rationale: Routing regressions and shadowed redirects are a specific, costly problem for developers and operators; the product directly addresses detection and safe change validation.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets redirect and rewrite failures across eleven hosts.
Visible stale-link/404 and first-match failure scenario.
creativity_rationale: A focused but fresh synthesis of redirect management, cross-host translation, and human-agent shared state.
creativity_evidence: Three-app concept spanning Console, Preflight, and Studio.
Shared human/agent rule table and migration proof framing.
usability_note: The table, simulator, and staged write controls appear understandable and task-oriented.
red_flags: No submitted video despite a video URL in the description; frame evidence appears to be captured promotional/demo material.
Eleven-platform coverage is asserted more broadly than shown.
standouts: Shared store and read/write approval semantics are unusually well aligned to the task.
advance_reason: Strong product evidence, substantial WebMCP delta, and a clearly valuable developer workflow.

one_line: An RTS about sending goals across an interstellar delay so an agent must act on intent rather than stale clicks.
what_it_does: Lets a player manage an Alpha Centauri colony through delayed Earth views and intent-based Daneel decisions.
leverage_rationale: The game mechanic makes direct UI control fundamentally unsuitable; structured intent tools are the core interaction needed to operate under a 4.37-year command horizon.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly contrasts delayed mouse commands with goals, constraints, and preferences.
Frame sheets show the colony strategy interface and Daneel/correspondence narrative surfaces.
execution_rationale: The screenshots establish a coherent strategy-game interface and narrative premise, but the central end-to-end intent interpretation and gameplay outcome are only partly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show repeated playable RTS views, colony map, HUD, and narrative/report screens.
Devpost media is a demo preview rather than direct observed execution.
impact_rationale: The game offers a credible educational and experiential way to communicate why agentic intent matters under extreme latency, even though its audience is specialized.
impact_evidence: Clear Asimov-inspired educational/demo purpose in the pitch.
Visible mission and colony-management presentation.
creativity_rationale: The interstellar latency premise turns WebMCP's intent model into the central game mechanic, producing a memorable and ambitious interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Alpha Centauri delay and stale Earth state are mechanically integrated.
Daneel receives goals and constraints rather than click sequences.
usability_note: The strategy interface is visible, but the delayed-intent workflow may require substantial explanation.
red_flags: No direct video evidence or transcript; intent execution is not visibly proven end to end.
standouts: WebMCP is dramatized as a necessary response to speed-of-light latency, not a bolt-on API.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and transformative WebMCP framing justify advancement despite incomplete execution evidence.

one_line: A job-search and application-preparation agent that fills supported workflows while reserving final submission for the candidate.
what_it_does: Finds and matches jobs, prepares applications from profile/resume data, fills forms, and pauses for human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured WebMCP application workflows can reduce repeated form friction and preserve a shared browser state, but general browser agents can achieve much of the same outcome.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies WebMCP interaction with supported application workflows in a real browser.
Devpost screenshot shows find/match, prepare, automate, and human-approve stages.
execution_rationale: The packet has polished positioning and mockup-like packaging but no video frame sheets or end-to-end execution evidence, so claimed automation cannot be credited strongly.
execution_evidence: Facts report no submitted video/frame sheets.
Devpost media shows workflow diagrams and UI mockups only.
impact_rationale: Job seekers face a real, repetitive, high-friction application process and retaining final approval addresses a meaningful trust concern.
impact_evidence: Clear candidate audience and repeated-form problem in the about text.
Explicit human-controlled final submission.
creativity_rationale: A competent and useful application of agents to job search, with human approval as a sensible safety angle but limited conceptual novelty.
creativity_evidence: End-to-end job discovery-to-prepared-application framing.
Human-in-control boundary is explicit.
usability_note: The staged workflow is easy to understand, though real job-site variability is unresolved in evidence.
red_flags: Core automation and supported-site coverage are asserted rather than demonstrated.
standouts: Clear human approval boundary for consequential submissions.
advance_reason: Good problem fit, but thin evidence and only a moderate WebMCP delta make the submission hard to advance.

one_line: A restaurant back office where agent writes become costed, blocking proposals that managers approve or reject.
what_it_does: Provides restaurant operations data and read tools, then gates every consequential write behind a computed proposal and human decision.
leverage_rationale: A blocking WebMCP write call that returns the manager's decision, with site-computed cost and shared live state, creates a collaboration pattern not comparably reproduced by generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes ten free read-only tools and six write tools that block until a human decides.
Video evidence shows proposal cost, supplier minimum, approval/rejection, and updated stock.
execution_rationale: The 108-second video transcript and frame evidence coherently demonstrate the central workflow, including rejected and approved changes, reversibility, and audit attribution.
execution_evidence: Transcript gives a complete order proposal, approval, rejection, and standing-approval flow.
Frame sheet shows restaurant dashboard, agent panel, approval controls, and tool activity.
impact_rationale: Restaurant managers have real financial, inventory, and operational risks; costed proposals and accountable approvals directly address the trust gap.
impact_evidence: Three-branch restaurant scenario with orders, stockout timing, supplier minimum, and cash consequences.
Every change records who asked and who agreed.
creativity_rationale: The product makes site knowledge and cost computation part of the agent confirmation contract, a deep and memorable alternative to generic confirmation dialogs.
creativity_evidence: Write calls remain unresolved until human decision and return the manager's reason.
Standing approvals are bounded by change type, cash ceiling, uses, and revocation.
usability_note: The proposal rail, approve/reject actions, explanations, and audit trail are clear and operationally legible.
standouts: Best evidence-backed human-agent write protocol in the packet.
Site-derived cost context makes approval meaningful rather than ceremonial.
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage, execution evidence, impact, and originality.

one_line: A visible daily workspace unifying work context with agent reads and approval-gated actions.
what_it_does: Combines email, tasks, calendar, notes, memory, accounts, activity, and a Shopify catalog in one workspace.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent typed access to shared workspace state and makes cross-domain reads and verified approved changes visible in one surface, though some general-agent substitution remains.
leverage_evidence: About text describes shared tools across email, tasks, calendar, memory, and Shopify.
Frames show Today dashboard, assistant panel, prepare-then-confirm flow, and product catalog/cart states.
execution_rationale: Multiple consistent frames show a coherent dashboard and staged workflow; the breadth of integrations is claimed more than fully demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show Today workspace, urgent-email/daily-brief workflow, and confirmation states.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows catalog results and Prepare cart controls.
impact_rationale: People with fragmented work across inboxes, tasks, calendars, and accounts have a clear need for a visible, calm coordination surface.
impact_evidence: Specific scattered-work problem described in the packet.
Synthetic public workspace includes urgent email, daily brief, and catalog/cart use cases.
creativity_rationale: The integrated visible workspace and consistent approval/audit model are a fresh synthesis, though the productivity hub category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Cross-domain daily workspace combines personal workflow and commerce actions.
Movable voice agent uses the same visible tools.
usability_note: The Today view, side navigation, assistant panel, and explicit confirmation states appear approachable.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct observed tool invocation in the packet.
standouts: Strong visibility and approval framing across heterogeneous work data.
advance_reason: Broad but coherent productivity use case with credible shared-state and approval evidence.

one_line: A football play designer whose agent finds spatial/timing risks and stages coach-approved repairs.
what_it_does: Edits and animates 11-on-11 plays, runs deterministic checks, focuses evidence, and previews tactical fixes before applying them.
leverage_rationale: Structured play state and deterministic spatial analysis let an agent identify exact timing and distance risks and stage a precise change more reliably than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies seven tools for reading state, running checks, focusing evidence, and staging repairs.
Frame/package evidence shows Before/After review and risk change from 2 to 1.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually complete play-design surface with editing, animation, analysis, preview, and export; direct end-to-end video evidence is absent.
execution_evidence: About text enumerates presets, routes, timing, undo/redo, import/export, and PNG export.
Devpost screenshot shows football field, route lines, assistant, and demo media.
impact_rationale: Football coaches have a concrete need to inspect timing and spacing risks in complex plays without surrendering tactical judgment.
impact_evidence: Specific 2.15-second/#52 spatial-risk example.
Coach-first framing and approval before playbook application.
creativity_rationale: The combination of deterministic tactical analysis, animated shared timeline, and staged coach review is a strong original interaction for the category.
creativity_evidence: Agent focuses exact evidence window rather than merely suggesting prose.
Before/After risk visualization and approval boundary.
usability_note: The field, timeline, and Before/After review support coach comprehension, though the tool is domain-specific.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheet directly proves the narrated tool sequence.
standouts: Deterministic spatial/timing diagnosis is a meaningful agent role without pretending to predict game outcomes.
advance_reason: Strong domain-specific leverage and impact with substantial product completeness evidence.

one_line: A conversational battery-shopping storefront that matches vehicles to products and carries context through quote and handoff.
what_it_does: Uses natural-language vehicle search, compatible battery comparison, quote cart, voice assistance, and visible catalog updates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP keeps the advisor and storefront synchronized and enables structured catalog/cart updates, but a general agent could reproduce much of the shopping flow with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes Gemini invoking native functions to update the visible catalog.
Frames show vehicle-specific battery results, assistant panel, product specs, and selection controls.
execution_rationale: The packet visibly demonstrates a coherent vehicle-to-battery catalog flow with product cards, specs, prices, and assistant context, though completed sale is not shown.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show Toyota vehicle context, multiple batteries, prices, and select buttons.
Devpost screenshot shows BateríasPower catalog and agent panel.
impact_rationale: Vehicle owners need compatibility confidence when buying batteries; guided matching and preserved context can reduce costly selection errors.
impact_evidence: Concrete Toyota Corolla compatibility scenario.
Product specifications and compatible-result presentation are visible.
creativity_rationale: Conversational automotive compatibility plus mobile-first advisor and human handoff is a useful fresh synthesis, though commerce assistants are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Unified advisor workspace carries vehicle, history, image, voice, and text.
Human handoff preserves conversation and selected product.
usability_note: Vehicle prompt, compatible cards, specs, and selection actions make the path understandable.
red_flags: Pitch promises completed sale, but evidence mainly shows informational quote/cart rather than payment completion.
standouts: Good product-context continuity between conversational guidance and storefront results.
advance_reason: Clear audience value and credible visible product flow, with meaningful though not transformative leverage.

one_line: An agent-native tabletop game where character abilities exist only as live, state-constrained WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Pairs a human player with an AI character whose speech and actions are dynamically registered according to traits, skills, and world state.
leverage_rationale: The live tool registry is the rules engine: unavailable abilities cannot be selected, making character constraints enforceable rather than prompt-adjudicated.
leverage_evidence: About text explains typed speech acts and action tools register/unregister as world and character state change.
Frame sheets show character cards, world/story screens, and tool-call/debug overlays.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent character-based web experience and detailed mechanics, but the registry transitions and complete play loop are only partially visible.
execution_evidence: Devpost demo preview shows map, character information, notes, and dialogue.
Frames show multiple character/story states and live-registry-related overlays.
impact_rationale: Solo tabletop players have a real desire for a principled second player rather than a permissive narrator; the game directly targets that niche.
impact_evidence: Specific solo tabletop audience and second-player problem.
Character refusal/limited abilities are central to the demonstrated concept.
creativity_rationale: Making tool existence, typed speech, and live registration the character's capabilities is genuinely novel and deeply integrated into play.
creativity_evidence: No free-text escape hatch; speech acts are constrained by registered tools.
World transition visibly unregisters old abilities and stamps in new ones.
usability_note: The editorial character presentation is coherent, but the constrained interaction model may require onboarding.
red_flags: No direct transcript; registry behavior is mostly asserted in the write-up and small overlays.
standouts: WebMCP capabilities become diegetic character abilities and enforce personality constraints.
advance_reason: One of the clearest transformative and creative uses of WebMCP in the packet.

one_line: A shared spatial canvas where a human and agent plan rooms and objects together in real time.
what_it_does: Represents rooms and objects as structured spatial data that both manual users and agents can create, move, resize, rotate, duplicate, and delete.
leverage_rationale: Structured geometry and shared canvas state make agent spatial edits more precise and inspectable than generic UI driving, though the same operations remain manually possible.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly lists shared structured spatial operations and concurrent human/agent editing.
Frame sheets show a canvas evolving through added and rearranged room/rectangle elements.
execution_rationale: The frames prove an evolving canvas and the packaging shows a room-layout interface, but the claimed practical bungalow generation and rich object operations are thinly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show iterative changes to a white spatial canvas with outlined components.
Devpost screenshot shows floor-plan grid and room layout demo preview.
impact_rationale: Event organizers, homeowners, and spatial planners can benefit from quickly visualizing and iterating layouts with an agent while retaining direct editing control.
impact_evidence: About text names houses, offices, events, restaurants, exhibitions, warehouses, and studios.
Bungalow layout example is described and visually previewed.
creativity_rationale: Shared agent-human manipulation of structured physical space is a fresh and useful interaction, though canvas planning itself is established.
creativity_evidence: Human can edit concurrently rather than wait for agent completion.
Agent performs the same spatial operations as the user.
usability_note: A canvas is an intuitive spatial metaphor, but sparse wireframe evidence limits confidence in finished usability.
red_flags: Frames are low-fidelity and do not clearly show a finished bungalow or robust spatial constraints.
standouts: Concurrent shared-canvas editing is a clear human-agent collaboration model.
advance_reason: Interesting shared-space concept, but execution evidence is comparatively thin and the leverage is not clearly transformative.

one_line: A local-first registry and runtime that turns reviewed action packs into bounded WebMCP tools inside an existing signed-in tab.
what_it_does: Binds reviewed manifests to exact origins and fingerprints, exposes allowlisted tools in the user's session, and gates writes with human authority and receipts.
leverage_rationale: It directly addresses the missing agent surface on existing authenticated sites, adding typed, bounded, reviewable capabilities without vendor APIs; this is precisely a new agent integration layer.
leverage_evidence: About text describes exact-origin packs, drift fail-closed behavior, declarative manifests, bounded untrusted output, and human-authorized consequences.
Frames show Action packs registry, Cal.com pack discovery, selectable actions, and result/state panels.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent registry/runtime concept with UI and code/demo evidence, but full security and cross-site operation are not independently observed end to end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show action-pack search, Cal.com details, execution steps, last result, and state.
Devpost media visibly packages Grafana/Calendar examples and the WebMCP demo.
impact_rationale: Operations teams commonly depend on authenticated systems without APIs; safely making those workflows agent-operable addresses a broad and concrete infrastructure gap.
impact_evidence: About text names monitoring, scheduling, payer portals, vendor consoles, and admin dashboards.
Registry and runtime explicitly target sites with zero native WebMCP registrations.
creativity_rationale: The login-as-API reframe, reviewed declarative action packs, drift fail-closed policy, and bounded untrusted output form an ambitious original infrastructure model.
creativity_evidence: Existing user session is reused without vendor API adoption.
Security and provenance controls are part of the product rather than afterthoughts.
usability_note: Registry search and action execution are visible, though pack authoring and trust review likely need significant operator expertise.
red_flags: Security/coverage metrics are presented in marketing slides and are not independently verifiable from the packet.
Real cross-site execution claims exceed the directly visible UI evidence.
standouts: Strong safety architecture around reviewed packs, exact origins, bounded output, and human authorization.
advance_reason: High-leverage agent infrastructure with a compelling and unusually safety-conscious adoption model.
